title: Hydrolysis and condensation of biomolecules
log: 2026-11-01T14:46:36Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new
2026-11-01T14:55:58Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: The closest bank point covers only condensation to form synthetic polymers such as nylon and PET, with no hydrolysis and none of the biomolecules (proteins, starch, glycogen, fats) or digestion that the new point requires, so it teaches a related but different idea.

draft.title: Hydrolysis and condensation of biomolecules
card: Two molecules join and a small molecule, usually water, is released. Cells use it to build large biomolecules from small units.
Amino acids join by condensation to form proteins. Glucose units join to form starch in plants and glycogen in animals. Fatty acids and glycerol join to form fats.
A large molecule is split by reacting with water. The water is used up, and the large molecule breaks into smaller units.
Digestion uses hydrolysis, helped by enzymes. Proteins break down to amino acids, starch and glycogen to glucose, and fats to fatty acids and glycerol.
draft.remember: Condensation joins units and releases water. Hydrolysis splits them and uses water.

a.q: Which change in the body is a condensation reaction?
opts: Glucose units joining to form glycogen
Starch breaking down to glucose in the gut
A protein breaking down to amino acids
A fat breaking down to fatty acids and glycerol
a.why: Glycogen is built by joining glucose units, and water is released. The other three changes break a large molecule into smaller units by reacting with water, so they are hydrolysis.
a.clue: Which change builds a larger molecule from smaller units?

b.q: Mia eats a meal of chicken and rice. In her gut, which reaction type and products match the digestion of the protein in the chicken?
b.why: Digestion breaks large molecules down by reacting them with water, which is hydrolysis. Protein is made of amino acids, so these are the products. Glucose comes from starch, not protein.
b.clue: Digestion splits large molecules. Which units make up a protein?

a.best: Glucose units joining to form glycogen
